args: Assess this NEW measured placement candidate: raise straight up, tilt about the identified short edge at the raised TCP (no yaw-only substitution), translate at that height, then lower vertically with the entire carton and fingers remaining above the inner lip. The visible short end is preferably lower. Check the supplied sampled rotation/swept envelope and the local route against the bottle, bowl exterior, plate and table. Check the available lateral finger-opening space above the bowl. Do not infer hidden clearance. Is this a supported local route with a plausible retained pinch during the tilt? Use English ASCII; unknown means unobserved, never a projected historical point.

bowl_mark_ids: b0: center of the large pale radial flower/star medallion on the visible interior floor.
b1: center of the separate smaller pale floral rosette on the bottle-side rear inner wall, above and beside the floor medallion.

context.gripper_policy: Keep closed through raise, tilt and transport; release only above the lip after fresh checks.

result.explanation: The visible scene and supplied rigid-carton model support the local closed-gripper raise, short-axis tilt and elevated transfer. The selected -1.2 rad tilt is not a yaw substitution and lowers the identified visible short end. The supplied minimum swept height becomes 0.981866 m after raising, or 0.976917 m after the between-sample reserve, above the 0.949636 m inner lip. The reported footprint margin is 5.03 mm versus the required 3.5 mm. The bottle is behind and to the side of this local route; the bowl exterior, plate and table are below the raised envelope. No external obstruction is visible in that route. Subsequent lowering is supported only while the entire modeled carton and fingers remain above the lip with uncertainty margins, not merely the TCP. A near-central opposed-side pinch is visually plausible, but retention throughout the tilt is not proven. This is not release authorization.

parameters.notes: Clear applies to the supplied local carton/finger envelope against visible external obstacles, not hidden geometry or whole-arm clearance. Visible lateral space has no observed external obstruction, but the robot self-occludes part of the bowl-side opening zone. The exact full-opening envelope and final lowering endpoint are not supplied. Complete opening clearance is therefore unobserved, not obstructed, and needs a fresh check before release. Opposing fingers visibly flank the carton; hidden contact areas, friction and future slip remain unknown. Closed fingers alone do not prove retention. The opposite short end and its corners are self-occluded and cannot be returned as current visible measurements. No earlier actual images are available here to independently verify retention during the logged lift. All returned pixels are selected on the current images, not inferred from historical projections. Bounding regions include multiple surfaces and require segmentation. Table regions measure visible surfaces, not free-space volumes.
